comment: Launch sim settings: time step, guidance, reliability, failure thresholds, orbit lifetime check and the launch/result screen text.
notes: Code generated with AI assistance (Claude). Reviewed by team. Read by scripts/sim/LaunchSim.gd, LaunchPlanner.gd and LaunchOutcome.gd, and by the Mission Control launch view (scenes/ui/launch). Units: SI (s, m, m/s, Pa) unless the key says km. GUIDANCE: the rocket rises vertically until it is moving at kick_start_speed_ms, tilts east to the pitch-kick angle over kick_ramp_s, then flies a gravity turn (nose follows the air-relative velocity). The kick angle is chosen by the guidance planner for every design (Cadet / Engineer) unless the design carries guidance.pitch_kick_deg (Flight Director). Small rockets whose upper stages are all kick stages (the same 'lofted' rule as delta_v_map.json loss_model) coast to the top of the booster's arc and fire the kick stages horizontally there, like Juno I. Other upper stages light straight after separation and steer along the velocity still to be gained (upper_law vgo: from the current velocity to a level circular orbit at the current height, with a gentle pull towards the insertion altitude, vgo_altitude_tau_s, and a hold against gravity, vgo_gravity_tau_s); upper_law linear is the older linear-guidance law (max_down_fraction, max_retarget_km, time_to_go_includes_burnout apply to it only). The planner flies at dt_s too, so its plan and the real flight match. The vgo constants were picked by one sweep over the Level 1 Easy rockets (all variants reached the same orbits; tau 200 s / 10 s gave the lowest, most efficient apogees). Liquid engines cut off once the orbit meets the mission target; solids always burn out. RELIABILITY: one roll per engine per flight (engines.json 'reliability', else the defaults here) and one per stage separation; a failed engine quits at a random moment of its burn. A Max-Q above warn_fraction of the structural limit (materials.json q_limit_model) rolls for a break-up, rising from 0 to structural_roll_max at the limit; above the limit it always breaks up. Every number here is MADE UP for gameplay unless its source says otherwise.

lifetime.formula: days = table(h_eff) x clamp(ballistic coefficient / reference, min_factor, max_factor); h_eff = perigee + apogee_weight x (apogee - perigee). Ballistic coefficient = payload mass / (payload_cd x payload side area); side area = payload length x top diameter (a tumbling satellite). Table from orbits.json lifetime_table, interpolated in log(days).
lifetime.source: MADE UP quick check. Drag happens mostly near perigee, so an elliptical orbit lives like a slightly higher circular one. Real Explorer 1 (358 x 2,550 km) stayed up about 12 years.

text.title: MISSION CONTROL  //  FLIGHT
text.poll_prompt: FLIGHT, all stations report. Press GO to start the count, HOLD to scrub and go back.
text.planning: GUIDO is working out the pitch program...

failure_types.no_liftoff: No liftoff: the engine could not lift the rocket's weight.
failure_types.unstable: Lost control: the rocket was not stable and tumbled in the thick air.
failure_types.structural: Structural break-up at Max-Q: the air pressure crushed the rocket.
failure_types.engine_out: Engine failure: an engine quit before its stage had finished.
failure_types.staging: Staging failure: the stages did not separate.
failure_types.no_orbit: Fell short of orbit: not enough speed by the time the fuel ran out.
failure_types.low_orbit: Orbit too low: the perigee dips into the air and the satellite comes down too soon.
failure_types.short_apogee: Fell short: the rocket did not climb as high as the mission needed.

text.lifetime_ok: Orbit lifetime about %s: more than the %d days the mission needs.
text.lifetime_short: Orbit lifetime only about %s: the mission needs %d days.
text.reason_max_q: Max-Q %.1f kPa of a %.1f kPa limit.
text.reason_margin_warn: Max-Q came close to the structural limit (%.0f%%).
text.reason_goal_perigee: Perigee %.0f km is below the %.0f km the mission needs.
text.reason_goal_apogee: Peak altitude %.0f km is below the %.0f km target.
text.reason_spare: Spare propellant at cutoff: %.0f kg (%.0f m/s).

max_q: Max-Q. Through the worst of it.
coast: Coasting up to the top of the arc.
orbit_achieved: FIDO: Apogee {apogee}, perigee {perigee}. We have an orbit!
failure_no_liftoff: BOOSTER: No liftoff! Shut it down!
failure_unstable: GUIDO: She's tumbling! We've lost her.
failure_structural: ...telemetry is static. We've lost the signal.
failure_staging: No separation! Stage is still attached!
failure_no_orbit: FIDO: We're not going to make orbit. Perigee is below the atmosphere, she's coming back down.
failure_engine_out: FIDO: Not enough left to make orbit after that engine.
